summary: Backend-only functional regression testing of the 6 N+1 query-batching rewrites (super_admin.list_orgs, admin.export_evidence, admin.export_cqc_excerpts, admin.export_cc_excerpts, admin.export_transcripts, dashboard.fetch_structure, review.share_meeting). Built a purpose-designed seed set (4 signed_off meetings: 3 with distinct analyses+transcripts, 1 with a DANGLING analysis_id AND transcript_id; one meeting carrying a PII redaction on a phrase that also appears verbatim in another meeting's transcript; a two-attendee meeting; a sign-off-manager-as-attendee meeting; 2 teams under one setting; a shared_reviewer user) plus 2 pre-existing meetings that legitimately SHARE the same analysis_id, then created a 31-test pytest suite that asserts exact row-level output (CSV tuple-for-tuple equality, PDF text extraction via pypdf) rather than just status codes. Result: 31/31 passed, 0 regressions, 0 5xx during the run. Verified: per-org user_count/meeting_count exactly match direct DB COUNTs for every org plus all scalar fields and name-ASC ordering; evidence CSV returns the full expected 12-row set for 3 meetings (no dropped/duplicated rows) with the dangling-analysis meeting silently skipped; PDF variant contains every meeting; staff_ids and date_from/date_to filters scope correctly; CQC/Care-Cert excerpt PDFs contain every regulation/standard ref computed independently from the DB, rejected mappings excluded, per-item excerpt/attendee/manager context correct; cc-excerpts staff_ids filter (moved before the batched fetch) excludes non-matching meetings AND excludes unselected attendees from the context line, filename reflects staff, unknown staff -> 404; transcripts export returns all 3 transcripts, dangling transcript_id skipped, and PII redaction stays strictly per-meeting (M1 body redacted, M2's identical phrase untouched, no cross-apply in the batched run); dashboard structure correct for org-level admin (all settings + all teams, name-sorted), setting-scoped manager (1 setting + both its teams) and team-scoped manager (1 setting + exactly 1 team), and an empty/nonexistent setting scope does not break ANY($1::text[]); share_meeting adds 2-3 mixed-role users in one request with the right count, adds only genuinely-new users on re-share, silently skips 'attendee' role, skips cross-org and nonexistent user_ids, and dedups the same user_id submitted 3x (added once). Also re-verified SEC-002 placeholder numbering on both scoped-manager export paths.
critical_code_review_comments: Verified safe: two pre-existing meetings share the same analysis_id (55ab6bf1...). export_evidence/cqc/cc all do `adoc = dict(a_row)` before `_apply_redactions_deep`, so the cached batched dict is never mutated in place — meeting-specific redactions cannot bleed between meetings sharing an analysis. Do NOT 'optimise' this into an in-place redaction on the cached dict.
Verified safe: dangling analysis_id / transcript_id rows fall through `if not a_row: continue` and are dropped from the export exactly as the pre-fix per-row fetch did (no 500, no partial row).

Pre-existing (unchanged by this fix, worth a separate ticket): export headers/context lines print attendee names and sign_off_manager_name straight from the meetings row WITHOUT applying pii_redactions, while the analysis/transcript body IS redacted. So a name redacted out of the transcript still appears in that same PDF's attendee line (confirmed in both cqc-excerpts and transcripts exports).

Pre-existing data-integrity nit: teams row 'Team Alpha' (1b9f4708-...) has setting_id NULL, so it is invisible in the dashboard filter dropdown both before and after the rewrite (the old per-setting loop excluded it too — not a regression). Either backfill setting_id or block NULL-setting teams at creation.

dashboard.get_dashboard uses asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) with a None default for fetch_structure, so any future exception inside the batched teams query would silently render an empty filter dropdown instead of surfacing an error. Consider logging the swallowed exceptions.

export_cc_excerpts still uses `WHERE id = ANY($1)` (untyped) for the staff-name lookup while every other batched call uses `ANY($1::text[])`. It works today because users.id is text, but the explicit cast would be more consistent/robust.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable suite: `cd /app/backend && python3 tests/_iter102_seed.py seed && python3 -m pytest tests/test_iter102_n1_batching.py -n 0 -q; python3 tests/_iter102_seed.py cleanup`. MUST use -n 0 (xdist workers race on the shared-account MFA override). The suite depends on the seed script — it will fail with KeyErrors if run without seeding. Gotchas learned: dashboard response key is `org_structure` (not `structure`); export-evidence/export-transcripts share a 10-per-hour rate-limit bucket keyed `export:<user_id>` in the login_attempts table (the suite's autouse fixture DELETEs login_attempts before every test); PDF assertions must be made on whitespace-squashed pypdf text; meetings/analyses/transcripts/teams/org_settings .id are all TEXT (users.id is text in public schema), so ANY($1::text[]) is correct. Backend .err.log tracebacks are benign uvicorn lifespan CancelledErrors; the three 500s in backend.out.log are from earlier sessions (lines 28-81 of 1079), not from this run.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional issue found. The two initial test failures were both defects in my own assertions, not the app: (1) I asserted on the wrong dashboard response key, and (2) I asserted the redacted phrase was absent from the whole transcripts PDF when it legitimately still appears in the un-redacted attendee header line (pre-existing behaviour) — the transcript body itself was correctly redacted. Both assertions were corrected and re-run green. A third initial failure came from a pre-existing teams row with a NULL setting_id, which the old per-setting-loop code also excluded, so it is not a regression.
